quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down as you approach the intersection. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 or older cannot legally drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp, a driver should:

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
Have the right-of-way.
Force their way into traffic.
Assume other drivers will move out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
questions.explanation: When entering an interstate from an entrance or acceleration ramp, yield to traffic already on the highway. Merge safely when you find an opening.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.
Oncoming traffic.
Pedestrians already in the intersection.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, and other drivers already in the intersection. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?

options.text: It is illegal to drive around lowered gates at a crossing.
You must stop when a flagger signals you to stop at a railroad crossing.
Not all railroad crossings have flashing lights and gates.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning devices like gates or flashing lights. Not all crossings have these devices. It is against the law to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
Only when driving in rural areas.
When driving under adverse weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you disrupt normal traffic flow. You can get a citation for driving too slowly.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: When you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, yield the right-of-way to that vehicle. You may proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?

options.text: Under no circumstances.
When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
Only when other vehicles yield.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red or blue light or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your hazard lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually and check the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Look for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Before turning left, signal 3 to 5 seconds ahead. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multi-lane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Wait for traffic and pedestrians to pass, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: At night, it is hardest to see:

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other drivers.
Street lights.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other objects along the road.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.
A driver must stop and proceed when the way is clear.
A driver must stop until a green light or green arrow appears.
A driver may turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver must stop until a green light or green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow shows, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: You may drive around the gates at a railroad crossing:

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.explanation: Stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagperson signaling, or a train horn. Never drive around a lowered gate.

questions.question: A green arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
You may proceed, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if a circular green light also appears.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may proceed, and you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may go, but you must turn in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: A single dashed white line separating traffic means:

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Lanes move in opposite directions.
Drivers may not pass.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross these lines to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is likely:

options.text: A deaf person.
Involved in a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog.

questions.question: This sign tells you:

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you of an upcoming winding road with three or more curves.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive faster than other vehicles.
Drive slower than other vehicles.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Drive with the flow of traffic, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Speed up.

questions.explanation: Unless a sign says no, you may turn right or left at a green light. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection when turning.
